div.head: Rect 21.4
div.ab: [21.4] Feola syndon folcgerihtu: on sumre ðeode gebyreð winterfeorm, Easterfeorm, bendform for ripe, gytfeorm for yrðe, mæðmed, hreacmete, æt wudulade wæntreow, æt cornlade hreaccopp 7 fela ðinga, ðe ic getellan ne mæig.

In quibusdam locis datur firma natalis Domini et firma paschalis et firma precum ad congregandas segetes et gutfirma ad arandum et firma pratorum fenandorum, hreaceroppum (id est macholi summitas) et firma ad macholum faciendum, in terra nemorosa lignum plaustri, in terra uberi caput macholi, et alia plurima fuerint a pluribus,

Feola syndon folcgerihtu: on sumre ðeode gebyreð winterfeorm, Easterfeorm, bendform for ripe, gytfeorm for yrðe, mæðmed, hreacmete, æt wudulade wæntreow, æt cornlade hreaccopp and fela ðinga, ðe ic getellan ne mæig.

Vielerlei sind die Gerechtsame des Volks [Leistungen der Herrschaft für die frohnenden Hintersassen]: in mancher Gegend gebührt Weihnachtskost, Osterkost, Kost bei Geheissfrohn zur Ernte, ‘Gussmahl’ [Trinkfest] fürs Pflügen, Mahtlohn, Heuschober-Essen, beim Holzverladen [von jedem] Wagen [1] Baum, beim Kornladen die Feimenkuppe und viele Dinge, die ich nicht aufzählen kann.

Many are the people's dues [the lord's provisions for the tenants doing labour-service]: in some districts are due a Christmas feast, an Easter feast, a feast at boon-work for the harvest, a ‘pouring-feast’ [drinking-feast] for ploughing, a mowing-reward, a rick-meal, at wood-carting a tree [from each] wagon, at corn-carting the top of the rick, and many things which I cannot recount.

The people’s rights are many: in some communities they are due a meal at Christmas, a meal at Easter, a feast at harvest, a feast for the plowing, a hayrick feast for the cutting of the grass, a log in return for the carting of wood, the topmost grain on the cart for the transportation of the crop, and many other things that I cannot list.
div.note: The Quadripartitus read ‘midwinterfeorm’ as in 9.1, probably better. ‘bendform’: the Quadripartitus read ‘benf[e?]orm’, after 4.1c (compare ‘andfeald’ VIII Atr 19 f.). The Quadripartitus translated ‘lāde’ (land) instead of ‘lade’ (carting), and avoids the first person (as 5.1). Liebermann compares Rect 9.1 and 5.4.
